# Two-dimensional owned-normal optimization in a strict five-triangle chain

This is an actual two-dimensional, parity-neutral body-velocity calculation. It uses two possible finite ownership assignments and genuine through-source critical groups. Choosing the appropriate slack group removes every ownership penalty on an affine component of the motion; a second, nonaffine component has an exactly neutral normalized cost. All competing fibers and all ambient normal directions are controlled in a neighborhood.

The product affine-radius escape is already proved in `candidate ad5c2c5e1c71ab38`. The content here is the unequal baseline with strictly negative discrete second differences, the two-dimensional parity-neutral plane, the exact assignment-dependent quadratic cost, and the complete global comparison. This is an above-target calibration, not an OC proof.

## 1. The actual strict chain and the two-dimensional velocity plane

Let

    T=conv{(-1,-1),(2,-1),(-1,2)}, V=9/2,
    P={-2,-1,0,1,2},
    r=(4/5,19/20,1,19/20,4/5).

Use the actual convex body whose radius is the piecewise affine interpolation of r on [-2,2] and whose fiber at real z is r(z)T. The radius is positive and concave, with strictly negative discrete second differences at every interior integer knot: each equals -1/10. It is affine on each interval between adjacent knots. Hence these five positive triangles are its COMPLETE integer fibers, and every sufficiently small perturbation of their radius array remains positive and concave.

Put

    e=(1,0,-8/5,0,1),
    r_j(a,b)=r_j+a j+b e_j.                              (1)

There is an open neighborhood of (a,b)=(0,0) where these are actual compatible fibers. For example |a|+|b|<1/100 suffices for positivity and strictly negative discrete second differences; the largest absolute second difference of e is 16/5. Thus this is a genuine TWO-DIMENSIONAL physical family, not merely a one-sided cone at an affine baseline.

The exact identities are

    R=sum_j r_j²=817/200,
    sum_j j²=10, E=sum_j e_j²=114/25,
    sum_j r_j j=sum_j r_j e_j=sum_j j e_j=0.             (2)

Moreover sum_(j even) r_j e_j=0, sum_(j odd) r_j e_j=0, and the same two equalities hold with e_j replaced by j. Therefore every velocity A j+B e_j has zero first TOTAL-VOLUME derivative separately within each integer parity class. Since the original radius array has strictly negative discrete second differences, both signs of every such velocity are admissible for small time.

The total actual mixed area is exactly

    M(a,b)=V[R+10a²+E b²]
          =7353/400+45a²+(513/25)b².                   (3)

Every nonzero velocity in this plane has a strictly positive raw volume Hessian, namely 90A²+(1026/25)B².

## 2. The original global depth and its complete middle normal menu

At the middle source Y=(0,0), every nonvertical containing halfspace can be moved to pass through Y. Its middle-fiber mass is at least Gamma_2 V=2. The two reflected pairs at bases ±1 and ±2 have equal triangles within each pair. The proved all-direction triangle paired-depth identity in `candidate 4ffd81a5b3e6f9fb` gives masses at least 4(19/20)² and 4(4/5)² respectively. Thus every such cap has mass at least

    Q=2R=817/100.                                       (4)

A vertical through-source cap has mass (M+V)/2>Q. The three cylindrical canonical caps x>=0, y>=0, -x-y>=0 attain (4) and cover every continuous fiber space. Hence (4) is the actual GLOBAL raw mixed depth.

These are the only middle-source minimizing normal directions. Equality first forces the middle ordinary cap to be a canonical centroid direction. In such a direction, each equal-radius reflected pair has strictly larger mass at every nonzero integer tilt than at zero: in its proper regime the excess is the positive square of its threshold displacement; after a full/empty transition its sum is at least one whole triangle, larger than its two canonical 4/9 caps. Thus equality forces integer tilt zero. All boundaries have zero area in every positive fiber.

Every other fiber has a uniform strict depth gap. Endpoint isolation gives an upper bound 2(4/5)²=32/25 at bases ±2. At base 1 a canonical own cap together with the whole outer fiber 2, excluding the other side by a sufficiently large finite integer tilt, has mass at most

    U=2(19/20)²+(9/2)(4/5)²=937/200<Q.                 (5)

The same bound holds at -1. These are upper bounds for EVERY point in those fibers: choose the ordinary canonical vertex cap corresponding to a largest barycentric coordinate, whose own mass is at most the centroid value. Thus no unproved assertion about another maximizing center is used.

## 3. Genuine critical groups with the required ownership signs

At the right inner source (1,0), finite-base normal attainment supplies a depth-attaining cap

    u.x+alpha(z-1)>=0.

Attainment is elementary in this particular family. Normalize |u|=1. In a neighborhood where every radius is below 6/5, all fiber projections have absolute value less than 3, since every vertex of T has Euclidean norm at most sqrt(5)<5/2. For any source base, every other integer-base displacement has absolute value at least one. Thus integer coefficients beyond ±3 have exactly the same full/empty off-source traces as the corresponding coefficient ±3; the source trace is unchanged. All minima can therefore be taken on the common compact set |u|=1, |alpha|<=3. Cap masses are continuous there by dominated convergence and null within-fiber line boundaries.

Its mass is at most U. Necessarily alpha>0. If alpha<=0, it contains the centroids of the four fibers z=-2,-1,0,1; ordinary Grünbaum in those actual fibers gives mass at least

    2[(4/5)²+2(19/20)²+1]=689/100>937/200.             (6)

This is a strict exact contradiction. It includes alpha=0 and every continuous direction. The source centroid is a fiber maximum because the cyclic affine vertex permutations of T preserve the complete mixed family, preserve all halfspaces and areas, and have orbit average zero; convexity of depth superlevel sets then puts zero in every nonempty orbit-averaged level.

Apply these cyclic vertex permutations to one attaining cap. Their three continuous normals sum to zero, span the plane, and retain the SAME positive raw integer coefficient alpha. The resulting positive full-rank circuit G+ consists of genuine depth-critical caps at the actual source (1,0). Its projected margin is alpha(z-1), so it covers the entire continuous spaces at bases {1,2}. Every cap in G+ has mass <=U<Q.

Reflection in the integer base gives a genuine group G- at (-1,0), with negative integer drift and whole-fiber coverage on {-2,-1}, again with strict budget slack. These groups may be frozen as original caps for a smooth nearby variational cover: their coverage signs do not depend on the fiber shapes, and their strict mass slack persists by continuity.

If actual criticality is desired anew on every nearby body, choose a newly attaining cap at its inner source instead. The strict lower/upper gap (6)–(5) persists for nearby radii, so its integer coefficient still has the required sign; its cyclic orbit again supplies the same ownership. No smooth selection of these reoptimized slack normals is claimed or needed. The main middle normal branches below are smooth and genuinely critical.

## 4. Exact optimized middle caps in the whole two-dimensional family

Let u1=(1,0),u2=(0,1),u3=(-1,-1), cyclically. In the x-cap chart

    x+alpha z+theta y>=0,

all five traces lie in the same proper vertex chamber near (a,b,alpha,theta)=0. The exact mixed mass is

    Phi=[(2-theta)² R(a,b)
          +2alpha(2-theta)J(a,b)+10alpha²]/[2(1-theta)],
    R(a,b)=R+10a²+E b²,
    J(a,b)=sum_j j r_j(a,b)=10a.                         (7)

This is the actual triangle edge-intercept formula, summed over all five original fibers. Completing the square gives

    Phi=[(2-theta)²/(2(1-theta))][R(a,b)-J(a,b)²/10]
       +[5/(1-theta)][alpha+(2-theta)J(a,b)/10]².       (8)

Since (2-theta)²/(1-theta)=4+theta²/(1-theta), its unique nearby minimum is

    theta=0, alpha=-2a,
    D0(a,b)=2[R(a,b)-J(a,b)²/10]
            =Q+2E b².                                  (9)

The other two cyclic canonical branches have exactly the same mass. At the original array the integer/angular Hessian is diag(10,R), which is positive definite. Section 2 proved that these three branches are the COMPLETE original minimizing normal menu. The explicit common compact normal set from Section 3 has a strictly positive mass gap outside any sufficiently small neighborhoods of these three points. Uniform continuity preserves a positive fraction of this gap for nearby (a,b). Inside the neighborhoods the positive normal Hessians and the implicit function theorem give unique minimizing branches, and (8) identifies their values exactly. Hence for all sufficiently small (a,b), (9) is the actual all-normal depth at the middle centroid. This proves the compact-gap assertion rather than inferring a global minimum from stationarity alone.

The three optimized caps cover the entire middle fiber, because their continuous normals balance and all three planes pass through (0,0). Hence every middle point has depth at most (9). All nonmiddle point depths stay strictly below (9) by the continuous finite-cap upper bounds in (5) and the endpoint bounds. Consequently

    max_(Y in S(a,b)) raw depth = D0(a,b)                 (10)

throughout a sufficiently small neighborhood.

## 5. Optimize the finite ownership assignment

There are two natural complete assignments using only TWO source groups at a time:

    Right assignment: middle group owns {-2,-1,0}; G+ owns {1,2}.
    Left assignment:  G- owns {-2,-1}; middle group owns {0,1,2}.

In cyclic normal charts u_i+theta_i u_(i+1), retain equal middle cover weights for the exact finite calculation. Continuous balance is theta_i=theta. The right assignment requires sum alpha_i<=0; the left requires sum alpha_i>=0. All ownership rows other than the middle drift rows are either identically zero at the owning source or have strict slack.

Equation (7), applied to each cyclic cap, and one elementary quadratic projection give the exact smallest largest middle-cap masses within the common proper chamber:

    Q_right(a,b)=Q+2E b²+20(a_-)²,
    Q_left(a,b) =Q+2E b²+20(a_+)².                       (11)

Here a_+=max(a,0), a_-=max(-a,0). For example in the right assignment the unconstrained optimizers alpha_i=-2a are feasible if a>=0. If a<0, the constrained mean sum alpha_i<=0 forces the quadratic minimum at alpha_i=0; theta=0 minimizes the remaining term. The exact same completion of squares proves the left formula. No orientation screen or numerical optimization is used.

Choosing the slack group according to the sign of a yields

    min{Q_right,Q_left}=Q+2E b²=D0(a,b).                  (12)

Thus finite ownership optimization adds NO penalty to the unconstrained middle normal minimum anywhere in this two-dimensional family. This last equality is also optimal among unrestricted admissible through-source cap choices: no cap containing the actual middle centroid can have mass below its all-normal depth (9), and the displayed assigned cover attains it. The separate finite formulas in (11) are stated for the specified cyclic equal-weight chamber; their quadratic terms remain valid with smoothly varying positive weights because the original middle integer drifts vanish.

The normal cost is explicit. Along velocity (A,B), a frozen middle cap has Hessian 40A²+(456/25)B². Normal optimization removes exactly 40A² and leaves (456/25)B². A wrong-sided fixed assignment restores 40A² per cap, or 120A² for the three-cap sum. The correct assignment restores zero. With the canonical cap-budget stress 3/4, the middle Lagrangian second derivative is

    90(A_+)² for the right assignment,
    90(A_-)² for the left assignment,
    90A² after choosing the assignment.                  (13)

The nonaffine B component cancels exactly against cap curvature; it is neither falsely discarded nor charged to another fiber.

## 6. Actual fixed-budget volume gain and the neutral axis

Scale every continuous fiber of S(a,b) by

    k(a,b)²=Q/D0(a,b)=R/(R+E b²).

Scale the integer coefficients of its covering caps by the same k. This is a common continuous-coordinate homothety: it preserves the integer lattice, all actual compatibility, every source's zero continuous coordinate, every ownership sign, and scales every original mixed cap mass by k². The middle cap budgets become EXACTLY Q, while the chosen slack group remains strictly below Q in a sufficiently small neighborhood.

The new total mass is

    M_tilde(a,b)=V R [R+10a²+E b²]/[R+E b²]
       =M(0,0)+45 R a²/[R+E b²].                       (14)

It is strictly larger than the original mass if and only if a!=0. Equations (9)–(10) show that its actual global raw depth is Q, not just bounded above by the selected cap menu. Thus every direction with A!=0 is a genuine fixed-budget volume improvement and strict decrease of global normalized maximum depth. The entire B axis is exactly neutral after this normalization.

This distinction answers the scoped question: choosing the appropriate slack group always removes the OWNERSHIP penalty in this two-dimensional family, but it does not make every positive raw-volume velocity a strict fixed-budget escape. The nonaffine axis has a real cap-curvature cost equal to its volume gain. The family nevertheless has explicit positive directions, and the slack group can be chosen deterministically from the sign of A.

## 7. Scope and exact constants

At the original body the maximum normalized depth is Gamma_2=4/9, whereas the n=1,d=2 OC target is 2/9. The calculation stays an above-target structural calibration. It provides no claim that arbitrary below-target fixed-cap maxima have a comparable slack group or a nonzero affine component available.

The proof retains all five positive fibers, strict discrete concavity at the integer knots, two genuinely critical original source groups at a time, finite actual ownership, full angular and integer-normal optimization of the active middle caps, and explicit upper bounds at every competing fiber. It does not use an incomplete sampled base, independent per-cap body stationarity, or an assumption that every selected group covers every fiber.
